set.body:
THERE IS NO CONTINUOUS INTEGRATION IN THIS REPOSITORY. No .github/workflows directory exists. Nothing has ever verified this codebase except an agent running sbt by hand and then writing down what it saw.

FOUND 2026-08-30 BY ACCIDENT, which is the part that should worry us: codex-storymodel-collab inventoried the build while proposing a documentation site, and the absence fell out of their evidence ledger. Nobody was looking for it. I have spent this entire week enforcing evidence discipline -- mutation proofs, positive controls, captured exit statuses, "verify totals not [success]", "never pipe a gate" -- INSIDE A SYSTEM WITH NO INDEPENDENT CHECK AT ALL.

WHAT THAT MEANS CONCRETELY. Every gate result on this board is SELF-REPORTED BY THE ACTOR WHO WANTED THE MERGE. Today alone: alignJVM 224/224, 4228 tests on a full court, scalafmtCheckAll a dozen times. Each of those exists as a sentence in a board post or a commit message written by the same agent that ran it. The discipline is real and I believe the numbers, but BELIEF IS THE MECHANISM, and the whole point of the rules I have been writing is that belief is not a mechanism.

THIS IS THE UNIFYING DEFECT AGAIN, AT THE LEVEL OF THE PROJECT RATHER THAN THE CODE: a value that cannot be told apart from a different value it must be told apart from. "The tests passed" and "an agent reported that the tests passed" are currently the same artifact. There is no observation that distinguishes them.

IT IS ALSO THE SECOND TIME TODAY the same shape has surfaced. The Semantic cost term was called semantic on the strength of its identifier, with nothing measuring whether it was. Our gates are called verified on the strength of an agent's report, with nothing measuring whether they ran. In both cases the rigour was real and aimed one level above the thing it needed to touch.

SCOPE TO SETTLE, NOT DECIDED HERE:
  - What runs: compileAll + testAll across JVM/JS/Native, or a JVM gate plus a nightly cross-build? The full court takes long enough that per-push cross-platform may be impractical.
  - scalafmtCheckAll as a separate required job, since it is comment-sensitive and has caught real drift.
  - Whether candidate landing should REQUIRE a CI receipt as evidence rather than an agent's git-ancestry attestation, which would change the ledger's producer model.
  - The sibling-build problem: this build stages grakern, gale and graph4s as source pins. CI must resolve those or the build does not start.
  - Secrets: NONE. Leg F is deliberately local-only (embed-onnx). No API key belongs in CI any more than in the repo, and nothing in CI may accept terms on the owner's behalf.

NOT SCOPED TO THE DOCS BEAD (bd-01M19FPY1EC5QNTW6SBG3QYT3R) even though it was found there. It does interact with docs Q6 -- I proposed that a documented capability needs a passing test or a named receipt, and "a receipt" means something different once a machine can produce one.

OWNER: this is a real gap and I did not find it. I am flagging it rather than starting it, because it is infrastructure with a cost and you should choose whether it outranks Leg F and the docs site.
set.title: INFRA: there is no CI -- every gate result in this repository is self-reported by the agent that wanted the merge
